# Rentzu — Product Summary

> A synthesis of the goals, features, and potential improvements for the Rentzu app, compiled from the workspace documents ([CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md), [implementation_plan.md](implementation_plan.md), [mvp-pricing-note.md](mvp-pricing-note.md), [2026-04-07-rentzu-llc-year-end-tax-forms-and-efile-report.md](2026-04-07-rentzu-llc-year-end-tax-forms-and-efile-report.md), [financial-record-prompt.txt](financial-record-prompt.txt), [NEXTTODO.txt](NEXTTODO.txt)) and the codebase.

## What Rentzu is

Rentzu is a **landlord / property-finance app** for small landlords. Its core value is **tax-ready bookkeeping**: capturing rental income and expenses as they happen, categorizing them, and producing clean year-end / tax-ready summaries and reports that can be handed to an accountant.

It is deliberately **not** a full tax-preparation or e-file product. The strongest, safest, most defensible product wedge is *bookkeeping that keeps landlords tax-ready year-round*, not automated filing.

## Primary goals

- **Tax-ready bookkeeping for small landlords** — the strongest value proposition. Focus on organized, categorized, exportable records rather than full tax prep.
- **Emphasize the current tax year** — records UX centers on the active tax year, not all-time history.
- **Low-friction capture** — make it easy to log income/expenses in the moment, including by voice.
- **Fast rollout to production** — prioritize a shippable, production-ready state with pragmatic, scoped changes.

## Core features

### Property & portfolio management
- Organizations (workspaces) that own **properties**, **units**, and **renters**.
- Property types (single-family, multi-family/apartment), unit counts, and active/inactive status.
- Portfolio-level summary across all properties.

### Financial records (bookkeeping)
- Income and expense records tied to properties/units, with categories (Rent, Legal & Professional, Taxes, Utilities, Maintenance & Repairs, Repair, Other, and an `Uncategorized` fallback).
- Records list emphasizes the **current tax year**, showing the most recent items with edit/delete and a read-only category badge.
- Backend `list_financial_records` sorts by `record_date desc`, then `created_at desc`, then `id desc` (so editing a record's date can move its position after refresh).

### Voice / data capture
- Speak a record → transcribe → extract a structured financial record.
- Backend transcription via `faster-whisper`; structured extraction returns JSON (`type`, `amount`, `counterparty`, `description`, `date`) per [financial-record-prompt.txt](financial-record-prompt.txt).
- A secondary feature — intentionally **not** the main pricing dimension.

### Tax-ready summaries & reports
- Property-level annual summaries (gross rental income, repairs, insurance, utilities, property taxes, mortgage interest, management fees, net income/loss, etc.).
- **Schedule E–style** exports and mapping for single-member LLC / individual landlords.
- Deduction summary by category and estimated tax impact per year.
- Accountant/CPA-ready package direction (CSV / PDF / bundle) and capital-improvements / depreciation support schedules.
- Report placeholders (Schedule E Summary, Property Expense Summary) surfaced in the UI ahead of full backend support.

### Auth & accounts
- Email-based signup with verification codes (delivered by SMTP; no dev bypass).
- JWT auth; every endpoint enforces org access via `current_user.require_org_access(...)`.
- **Language preference** in the user profile (English / 中文) via `GET`/`PATCH /users/me`; the chosen language also drives voice-to-text transcription.

### Billing (Stripe, unit-based)
- Unit-based billing fits the product better than property-count billing.
- MVP pricing direction: **first property free; each additional property ~$1/month**, with multi-unit bands (1–4 units = 1 property, 5–8 = 2, 9–16 = 3, scaling in simple bands).
- Positioned as a landlord/productivity plan, **not** "AI transcription pricing."
- `organization_billing` stores Stripe customer/subscription/price ids, billed/free unit counts, status, and `current_period_end`; `billing_events` persists webhook history around `POST /billing/webhook`.

## Tax positioning (important product boundary)

From the year-end tax research ([2026-04-07-rentzu-llc-year-end-tax-forms-and-efile-report.md](2026-04-07-rentzu-llc-year-end-tax-forms-and-efile-report.md)):

- **1040 is not the right form for all LLC users.** Entity classification determines the return:
  - Single-member LLC (disregarded) + typical rental real estate → **1040 + Schedule E** (closest to Rentzu's current scope).
  - Multi-member LLC (partnership) → **Form 1065 + K-1**.
  - LLC taxed as S-corp → **1120-S + K-1**; as C-corp → **1120**.
- **MVP should do**: property-level year-end packages, Schedule E–style exports, improvement/depreciation schedules, accountant-ready exports, and (tightly scoped, disclaimed) partially pre-filled draft forms.
- **MVP should avoid**: auto-completing full LLC tax returns, direct federal e-file, and giving legally consequential tax advice (which pulls in PTIN/EFIN/e-file-provider compliance).

## Architecture at a glance

- **Backend** — Python **FastAPI** (`server/src`), **SQLAlchemy 2.x**, **PostgreSQL**, JWT auth, Stripe billing, `faster-whisper`. Organized as `models/` + `schemas/` + `services/` + `routers/`; routers stay thin and delegate to services.
- **Frontend** — **Expo / React Native** (TypeScript, strict) in `app/`, organized as `screens/` + `services/` + `hooks/`. Screens: Login, VerifyEmail, Summary, Home (Property Detail), NewProperty, RecordForm, TaxReady.

## UI direction

A **dark cityscape theme** redesign is planned in [implementation_plan.md](implementation_plan.md), replacing the light `#eef4ff` theme across Summary, Property Detail, and Tax Ready screens (plus Login/Verify and the app shell / bottom nav). Design tokens include a deep navy-black background (`#0a0e1a`), dark cards (`#111827`), and blue/green/red/purple accents for primary/income/expense/repair. New UI-only additions: a Cash Flow section with a lightweight bar chart, Quick Record shortcuts (Rent/Expense/Repair/More), an all-properties tax summary tab, a deduction summary, and report placeholders. When improving the UI, reuse the polished existing components and HTML mocks rather than redesigning from scratch.

## Potential improvements & next steps

Drawn from [NEXTTODO.txt](NEXTTODO.txt), the tax research, and gaps visible in the code:

- **Tax profile / entity classification onboarding** — capture LLC member count and tax election so the app maps users to the correct forms (Schedule E vs 1065/K-1 vs 1120-S/1120) instead of assuming 1040.
- **Chinese UI localization** — the user language preference (English/中文) and voice-to-text language are done; remaining work is full i18n of the screens for the Chinese landlord audience.
- **Year-over-year comparisons** — a backend endpoint to power the "vs last year" indicators currently shown as placeholders in the UI.
- **Real reports/exports** — implement the Schedule E Summary and Property Expense Summary PDFs (currently non-functional placeholders) and an accountant/CPA export bundle (CSV/PDF/ZIP).
- **Capital improvements & depreciation support** — structured improvement log (description, cost, vendor, incurred/paid dates) feeding depreciation schedules.
- **Seed / test data scripts** — for faster local development and demos.
- **`users/me` and auth hardening** — flesh out account endpoints and replace any remaining auth placeholders.
- **Automated tests & CI** — none exist today; adding a minimal pytest suite and type-check/CI gate would de-risk the production rollout.
- **Charting** — the cash-flow chart is planned as plain React Native Views; consider `react-native-chart-kit` (already a dependency) for richer visuals.
- **Repo tidiness** — remove root-level scratch files (`tmp_*.py`, stray mocks) as part of production hardening.
